doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Closing thanks and goodbyes
summary: Rowe hopes to bring him back to the Northeast; Berroa offers his knowledge to institutions and they say goodbye.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well this has just been a delight again, and I wish you the best of luck with your move and we’ll have to figure out a way to bring you back to the Northeast.

Well man it would be my pleasure. This is the way I sell myself. I have a lot to give. I think I have some knowledge and experience to share. It depends on the people at the differing universities and music institutions to take advantage of what I can offer. It’s like a lot of people ask me, “Hey Ignacio, when are you coming to this place?” I said, well the first thing I need is an invitation. If you don’t invite me to your house I won’t knock on your door, “Hey man, here I am.” I’m not going to be after you, “Hey can you invite me to your house? Can you invite me to your house?” That sounds like begging. So here I am, I’m here. I’m here. So it would be — I’d be delighted of going anywhere where people think that my knowledge and my experience is going to serve a purpose for the institution for the students, for people in general.
All right. Well thanks again and I’ll see you on the flip side.
Thank you, Monk, it was very nice. Thank you for having me. It’s been a pleasure. And to whomever listens to this interview, sorry for my English.
Well I’ll say again, we are jealous of the fact that you can speak in two languages and more of us should be able to do that. So there you go. © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
